issue.title: test_interruption_kills_process_group_with_pipe_holding_descendant[False] reads descendant.pid before the grandchild can write it under a 50 ms timeout

task_type_fields.evidence:
Proposed by phase sase-1no.6 (epic sase-1no, PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP note #1): during that phase's `just check` the `[False]` param failed once with `FileNotFoundError` on `descendant.pid`, then passed on rerun on an unchanged tree. Unrelated to the stranded-work epic, which never touches `sase.sdd`.

Likely root cause (from reading the test, triaged by the sase-1no land agent): in the `external_drain_alarm=False` case, `run_sdd_git(..., timeout=0.05)` can time out and kill the wrapper's process group before the grandchild `pipe-holder.py` interpreter has started and written `descendant.pid`. Python startup under a loaded parallel lane often exceeds 50 ms. Then `int(pid_file.read_text())` raises `FileNotFoundError` instead of proving the descendant was reaped. The wrapper already prints `child.pid` to stdout before it sleeps, so the test could read the pid from captured output, or wait for the pid file to exist before the timeout can fire.

Fail rate: 1 observed failure, then passed on rerun; observed in the parallel `just check` lane, not reproduced serially.

issue.creation_reason: Phase sase-1no.6 recorded a one-off FileNotFoundError on descendant.pid in just check that passed on rerun; the sase-1no land agent found no existing bead and traced a probable startup race in the test.

evidence.note: Independent recurrence in monitor s5y9d6mrs0eg (2026-10-24), check ToolRun f828e8358ca62f99b9d51921556a45f2: test_interruption_kills_process_group_with_pipe_holding_descendant[False] failed at pid_file.read_text with FileNotFoundError for descendant.pid in the 14-worker suite.
